To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) parents of young children in Hong Kong are more likely to vaccinate their young children against influenza if they believe that vaccination is safe, have a positive social norm about vaccination, and have vaccinated their child in the previous year; (2) parents who have never vaccinated their young children against seasonal influenza are more likely to do so in the future if they believe that the influenza vaccine is safe and if they perceive that other people vaccinate their young child against seasonal influenza; and (3)

the psychosocial factors that influence parental decision-making regarding seasonal influenza vaccination for young children in Hong Kong include beliefs in vaccination safety, social norms, and past vaccination history.
Child’s past influenza vaccine history, belief in vaccine safety and social norm are the main factors influencing parents’ decision on vaccination for their children.
